newsitem.title: USA: Calif. aims to create Internet college courses.
newsitem.headline: Calif. aims to create Internet college courses.

text.p: California said on Wednesday it was launching an initiative to create and market college courses and degrees through the Internet and other emerging technologies.

Breaking ranks with its neighbours, Gov. Pete Wilson, a Republican, said California would not join in a consortium of western states that are working on a similar scheme called the Western Governors University.
"California is uniquely positioned to become a world leader in the development and distribution of college-level software, courses and programmes," Wilson said.

Wilson instructed his deputy chief of staff to form a design team in consultation with leading universities in the state. He said the team would seek to create and market college courses through the Internet and other multimedia technologies for state, national and international markets.
University of California President Richard Atkinson welcomed the announcement, calling it a step in the right direction for California.
